chapter_title: The Three Earths that Exist, they bear Fruit.
chapter_note: The chapter begins with a brief dialogue-frame formula and then presents a compact, systematic “three earths/fields” teaching. Paragraphs 1–3 remain within cosmos→cosmos correspondences (earth/field ↔ farmers ↔ ascent mechanics). Paragraph 4 is an editorial seam that extends the pattern to the institutional “holy church” (elect/catechumens) and is therefore pastoral. Paragraph 5 is explicit exhortation/application to the audience and is pastoral.

paragraphs.core_text: Three earths exist in the universe, and are being toiled over. At first they [...] the farmer in them. Afterwards they bear [good] fruit to they who toil over them.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again he speaks to his disciples:” (late hagiographic container).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame-style incipit (“Once again… to his disciples”) introduces an older, impersonal, enumerative teaching (“Three earths exist…”) that sets up a systematic correspondential schema.

paragraphs.core_text: One of them is this great earth that people are living upon. They are ploughing in it [...], it with iron hoes, they cultivate, [making] the furrows, turning it over [...] Afterwards they harvest fruit from [it ...
paragraphs.temporal_note: Remains descriptive and structural (field + cultivation + harvest) without audience exhortation or institutional identification; functions as the first term in the three-fold correspondential set.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.245⟩
The second field is the living soul, the holy one. It is mixed in the entire zone, above and below. The farmers who toil over it are these two great light-givers, which journey through the heavens. They are toiling and cultivating it, so that they will draw it towards their aspect. And it leaps up and comes to the heights. It goes upwards, out from every place wherein it is, and it adds to them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear cosmos→cosmos mapping: living soul as a “field,” sun and moon (the “two great light-givers”) as its farmers, with ascent mechanics described impersonally. This is characteristic systematic substrate exposition.

Editorial seam/extension: applies the “third earth/field” slot to the institutional holy church and its ranks (“elect,” “catechumens”), shifting from cosmological mechanism to community-identification; even though “Light Mind” is cosmological, the paragraph’s mapping crosses into church structure.

Direct application voice and imperatives (“You yourselves…,” “Preach and enlighten…,” “Rather, toil!”) aimed at behavior and mission; this is late pastoral exhortation built on the preceding teaching.
